主要内容: The 2007 foreign oil asset expropriation in Venezuela had significant implications for U.S. oil majors, particularly Exxon Mobil (XOM) and ConocoPhillips (COP). On October 9, 2014, ConocoPhillips filed for arbitration against Venezuela's state-run oil company PDVSA, seeking compensation for its nationalized oil projects. This filing followed an already-pending arbitration case before the World Bank's ICSID (International Center for Settlement of Investment Disputes). In September 2013, an ICSID tribunal ruled in favor of ConocoPhillips, calling the Venezuelan government's action 'unlawful expropriation.' ConocoPhillips' stock fell 3% on October 9, following the compensation ruling in favor of Exxon Mobil in the Venezuelan asset expropriation case. ConocoPhillips had significant investments in the Petrozuata and Hamaca heavy crude oil projects, and the offshore Corocoro development project in Venezuela. In May 2007, the government expropriated all of ConocoPhillips' operations without fair compensation. Other major upstream oil companies affected by the 2007 expropriation include Chevron Corporation (CVX) and Total SA (TOT). XOM, COP, and CVX are components of the Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE). Despite the incident, Venezuela remains an important trade partner for the U.S., particularly in the oil and gas sector.
